episode.title: Bound summarizer input in one forward pass and restore accurate tail-budget accounting
episode.before: At parent dc2d7b1dfe76b46a371e897aff76c3af76c73dd0, ChatSummary.summarize_real split oversized history into a head and preserved tail, then reversed both the head messages and their token-size pairs, accumulated messages from the end of the head up to the summarizer model's input limit, and reversed the retained messages again before summarizing. It also replaced the full sized-message list with the head-only slice and subsequently calculated tail_tokens from sized[split_index:], which was empty after that truncation; consequently the final fit decision did not account for the preserved tail's tokens.
episode.after: At 188e9e1114f0dfdeb95f9b1592bc81777a8226fa, summarize_real retains the full tokenized-message list, creates sized_head for the head, and selects a model-input-bounded prefix by accumulating (tokens, message) pairs directly in original order without list reversals. It computes tail_tokens from the untouched full sized list, returns summary plus tail only when their combined token count is below max_tokens, and otherwise recursively compacts the combined result with the existing depth guard.
episode.diff: The single-file implementation change in aider/history.py replaces head/sized reversal and index-based selection with a forward iteration over sized_head; preserves the original sized list; changes tail-token calculation to sum the original slice beginning at split_index; and keeps the existing 4096-token metadata fallback, 512-token safety reserve, direct-return threshold, and recursive compaction path. No tests were changed in the commit.

evidence_units.claim: Commit 188e9e1114f0dfdeb95f9b1592bc81777a8226fa has parent dc2d7b1dfe76b46a371e897aff76c3af76c73dd0, is titled "Optimize head‑truncation loop in `summarize_real`", and modifies only aider/history.py.
evidence_units.source: git show --format=fuller --stat 188e9e1114f0dfdeb95f9b1592bc81777a8226fa; issue-bundle.json resolved_commit, parent_commit, changed_files_name_status

evidence_units.claim: The parent implementation sliced sized down to the head, reversed head and sized, accumulated entries by index up to model_max_input_tokens, and reversed keep before calling summarize_all.

The changed implementation removes the list reversals and index loop, introduces sized_head = sized[:split_index], and accumulates tokens and messages directly with `for tokens, msg in sized_head` until the model input limit would be exceeded.

Because the parent reassigned sized to its head slice before evaluating `sized[split_index:]`, its tail-token sum was empty; the changed implementation leaves sized intact and calculates the preserved tail's tokens from the original `sized[split_index:]`.
evidence_units.source: git show 188e9e1114f0dfdeb95f9b1592bc81777a8226fa^:aider/history.py and git show 188e9e1114f0dfdeb95f9b1592bc81777a8226fa:aider/history.py, ChatSummary.summarize_real

evidence_units.claim: The implementation derives the summarizer input ceiling from the first model's max_input_tokens, falls back to 4096 when undefined, and reserves 512 tokens before selecting messages for summarize_all.

After summarizing the selected head, the implementation returns summary plus preserved tail only if their token total is below max_tokens; otherwise it recursively invokes summarize_real with depth incremented, while the existing depth greater than three guard eventually summarizes all remaining messages.

Application startup constructs ChatSummary with the weak and main models and with the configured or model-default maximum chat-history token budget, making summarize_real part of runtime chat-history compaction.

candidate_atomics.name: select-bounded-compaction-prefix
candidate_atomics.title: Select summarizer input with one bounded forward pass
candidate_atomics.description: Choose a prefix of the compactable history head whose cumulative token count stays within the summarizer model's input capacity after a safety reserve, without reversing parallel message and size collections.

semantic_action.intent: Construct a bounded summarizer request while eliminating reversal-based traversal and keeping message order explicit.
semantic_action.pre_state: An oversized conversation has been divided into a compactable head and a preserved tail, and each message has a known token count.
semantic_action.post_state: The selected head input is an original-order prefix whose cumulative tokens do not exceed the first summarizer model's declared or fallback capacity minus the safety reserve.
semantic_action.validation: Use messages with distinct identities and token weights, capture the input passed to the summary operation, and assert original ordering plus cumulative size at or below the effective model-input ceiling; static diff inspection confirms the forward accumulation but the pinned suite lacks this targeted oracle.

candidate_atomics.name: reconcile-summary-with-preserved-tail-budget
candidate_atomics.title: Account for preserved context before accepting compaction
candidate_atomics.description: Measure the generated summary together with the untouched tail and recurse when their combined size still exceeds the configured history budget.

semantic_action.intent: Prevent a compaction result from being accepted based on a token calculation that omits the context being preserved.
semantic_action.pre_state: A head summary has been produced, a tail is being preserved verbatim, and the full tokenized-message sequence remains available.
semantic_action.post_state: The summary-tail result is returned only when its combined token count is below the configured history budget; otherwise the combined result re-enters bounded compaction.
semantic_action.validation: Construct a case where the summary alone fits but summary plus tail does not, then assert that recursive compaction occurs; construct a combined-fit case and assert direct return. The corrected slice is directly visible in the diff, but no targeted pinned test supplies this behavioral oracle.

candidate_workflows.name: compact-oversized-history-with-two-level-budgeting
candidate_workflows.title: Compact oversized history within both model-input and retained-context budgets
candidate_workflows.description: Bound the head sent to the summarizer, preserve the recent tail, and evaluate the combined result against the conversation-history budget before returning or recursively compacting it.

workflow_graph.goal: Produce a compacted conversation that respects the summarizer request capacity and does not accept a summary-plus-tail result whose measured size exceeds the configured retained-history budget.
when_to_use: Conversation history exceeds its configured retained-token budget and can be divided into a head to summarize and a recent tail to preserve.
The summarizer model has a finite input capacity that may differ from the retained-history budget.
anti_goals: Do not change the summary prompt, model-fallback behavior, or role filtering performed by the summary operation.
Do not discard or summarize the selected recent tail merely to simplify accounting.
Do not treat fewer list operations as sufficient validation of message-selection semantics or budget correctness.
not_applicable_when: The complete history already fits and the top-level compaction call can return it unchanged.
The history is too short to split safely or the recursion-depth guard requires summarizing the remaining history as one unit.
No token-count function or summarizer input-capacity information, including an explicit fallback, is available.
inputs: ordered conversation messages with roles and content
summarizer model input maximum or fallback
workflow_graph.entry_state: The full history exceeds the retained-history budget, a recent tail fitting approximately half that budget has been identified, and the split has been adjusted so the compactable head ends at an assistant boundary.
workflow_graph.exit_state: A head summary and preserved tail are returned only after their combined measured tokens fit the retained-history budget, or the existing bounded recursion/fallback path performs further compaction.

steps.condition: The head contains enough messages to summarize separately and recursion depth has not exceeded the guard.
steps.validation: Captured summary input preserves the selected messages' original order and stays within model input capacity after the reserve.

steps.condition: A head summary was successfully produced while a tail remains preserved.
steps.validation: The direct-return branch is taken only when summary tokens plus the full preserved-tail token sum are below the history limit; otherwise recursion receives summary plus tail.

validation_ladder: Inspect the diff to confirm token-size data for the full history remains available after deriving the head slice.
Unit-test bounded head selection with distinguishable messages and boundary token sizes.
Unit-test both combined-fit and combined-overflow branches, including an assertion that tail tokens are nonzero and influence recursion.
Run tests/basic/test_history.py and then the broader history/coder test suite in an environment with project test dependencies installed.
stop_conditions: Stop and use whole-history summarization when the split index is at or below the minimum safe split.
Stop recursive splitting and summarize the remaining messages together when the existing depth guard is exceeded.
Do not accept the change as behaviorally validated if only static inspection or the broad pre-existing summarize test is available.
unresolved_or_deferred: The commit provides no targeted regression test for head-selection order or corrected tail accounting.
The test suite could not be executed in the supplied environment because pytest is unavailable.

The change from selecting a suffix of the head after reversal to selecting a prefix in original order is observable, but repository evidence does not explain whether that semantic change was intentional or only an optimization side effect.

unresolved_questions: Was changing the selected summarizer input from the newest model-fitting suffix of the head to the oldest model-fitting prefix intentional? The commit title and unavailable PR discussion do not establish that design decision.
No targeted test proves the corrected tail-budget branch or the changed head-selection order, and local execution was unavailable because pytest is not installed.
